clue.text: Pain also leads to article about account given by hospital

indicators.note: 'about' puts the article round the next pieces, enclosing them

blocks.note: also means too
the definite article
AC is the usual abbreviation for account
H for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital visit about a billing dispute, where the pain is financial as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pain' at the start looks like a general complaint, but it is the definition; 'leads to' just joins the first piece to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothache is a specific kind of pain, so the general word stands for it as an example.

clue.text: A degree in part turning up as a deficit

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word from bottom to top, so backwards
'in' places the first pieces inside the other word

blocks.note: taken as written
DEG is the standard abbreviation for degree
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: A student admits that part of their degree went badly, leaving a shortfall.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted letters go between the second and third letters of the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade gap is a nation's shortfall when imports exceed exports, a kind of deficit.

clue.text: Contraption of pipes emptied over grain regularly

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving just the outside letters
regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here every other one

blocks.note: the first and last letters of over
first, third and fifth letters of grain

explanation.surface: A plumbing contraption pours out grain at steady intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe organ is an instrument built from ranks of pipes, so it is a contraption of pipes.

clue.text: Support performances around some trees – they're useful for chase scenes

indicators.note: 'around' means the first two pieces go on either side of the trees

blocks.note: to give a hand is to support
a brake is a thicket, a clump of trees or bushes
a turn is a stage act or performance

explanation.surface: Backing for stage acts set among woodland, with a nod to film-makers' car chases.
explanation.walkthrough: HAND and TURNS together surround BRAKE. Brake in the sense of thicket is old-fashioned but in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning a car round with the parking brake is a stunt-driving staple, so such manoeuvres serve chase sequences.

clue.text: British islands forbidding reservoir

blocks.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands
forbidding in the sense of grim and severe

explanation.surface: British islands are banning a reservoir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbidding' looks like a verb but is an adjective meaning stern. The Channel Islands lie off the French coast but are British Crown dependencies.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a tank for holding water, a small storage reservoir.

clue.text: Shade filling each old drain

indicators.note: something filling goes inside the other pieces

blocks.note: EA is the abbreviation for each
a tint is a shade of colour
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Colour seeping into every old drainpipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drain' reads as a noun beside the pipe-like surface, but the definition is the verb, to deplete.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat into savings is to use them up gradually, which is to drain them.

clue.text: Pondered laying off millions no longer in prime condition

indicators.note: laying off staff removes them, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: to muse is to ponder
M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: A business owner thought about cutting millions from a firm past its best.
explanation.walkthrough: Take M from MUSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something used is second-hand and worn, no longer fresh or in mint condition.

clue.text: Consequence of baking regulation upset King visiting coastal region

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read upwards
a visitor goes inside, so these pieces go within the region

blocks.note: an act is a law or regulation
K is the chess abbreviation for king
the shore is the coastal strip

explanation.surface: A monarch's seaside tour upsets the rules, with knock-on effects from some baking.
explanation.walkthrough: The turned regulation and the king both go inside the coastal word, just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortcake is a crumbly biscuit or cake, the product that results from baking.

clue.text: Source of theatrical effect – risk bringing in railway

indicators.note: bringing something in places it inside the other word

blocks.note: to dice with death is to risk it
RY is a standard abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A stage technician gambles on using the railway for a special effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dice with death' is the idiom that makes dice mean risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid carbon dioxide gives off the low-lying fog used on stage, so it produces that effect.

clue.text: Ridiculous car Tatler chose as one for the smart set?

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurd and disordered, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The society magazine Tatler picks an absurd car for its fashionable readers.
explanation.walkthrough: Tatler is a British society magazine. A Chelsea tractor is a mocking British name for a big 4x4 driven around posh Chelsea in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The term pokes fun at wealthy urbanites' off-road vehicles, so it is the car of choice for fashionable people.

clue.text: Have disappeared after repeatedly extracting energy for gas

indicators.note: extracting pulls something out, and doing it repeatedly means twice over

blocks.note: 'are gone' is another way of saying have disappeared
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Something has vanished after energy was drained from it again and again, to make gas.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove both Es from ARE GONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a noble gas, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Determined those people will accept alternative work on collections?

indicators.note: accepting something takes it inside

blocks.note: set on something means determined
they means those people
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Resolute workers will take on an alternative job dealing with collections.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: in mathematics a set is simply a collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Set theory is the branch of mathematics studying sets, which are collections of objects.

clue.text: Improve status of the French, after reflecting what's good for France

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is read backwards
'after' places the first piece behind the second

blocks.note: bonne is French for good (feminine)
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French people looking back on what is good for their country, and raising its standing.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to raise them to the nobility, lifting their rank.

clue.text: Turned in first item for auction – cartouche initially from Egypt?

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so read backwards
initially means taking just the first letter

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned
Lot 1, the first lot in an auction
first letter of cartouche

explanation.surface: An auctioneer's opening lot is a cartouche from Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: Lot 1 is written LOT I with the Roman numeral. The question mark flags a definition by example: Nilotic means of the Nile, not Egypt as such.
explanation.definitionFit: Nilotic means relating to the Nile, the river at the heart of Egypt, hence a fair hint.

clue.text: Moving ahead, along with map identifying both ends

indicators.note: moving letters around shifts their positions

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; 'with' adds the next word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pressing on with a map that marks the start and finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha and omega are the first and last Greek letters, so together they mean the beginning and the end.

clue.text: Couple possessed of such wild happiness initially will require this conveyance

indicators.note: wild suggests running out of control, so the letters are scrambled
initially takes the first letter only
possessing something means holding it within

blocks.note: a couple is a pair
taken as written
first letter of happiness

explanation.surface: A couple overjoyed at a new baby will need a buggy.
explanation.walkthrough: A pushchair is the British word for a stroller.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushchair is a folding seat on wheels for a small child, a conveyance pushed along.

clue.text: City is but a shell of London, after redevelopment

indicators.note: a shell is the outer casing, so only the outer letters are kept
redevelopment rebuilds things in a new layout, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
first and last letters of London

explanation.surface: A city reduced to a hollow version of London after being rebuilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul is Turkey's largest city, an example of the general word.

clue.text: Reliability: function supplied by stronghold

blocks.note: stead means role or function, as in 'stand in good stead'
a fastness is a fortress or secure refuge

explanation.surface: A fortress's job is to be dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: Stead and fastness are both somewhat old words; each is in standard dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfastness is firm loyalty and constancy, which amounts to dependability.

clue.text: Legal document about poor service that's cancelled

indicators.note: 'about' places the document around the other piece

blocks.note: a deed is a signed legal document
in tennis a let is a serve clipping the net, so it must be retaken

explanation.surface: A contract dispute over bad customer service leads to cancellation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor service' sounds like a complaint about a shop; it is a tennis serve that clips the net. DE(LET)ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deleted has been struck out or removed, so it is cancelled.

clue.text: I intend turning up to block a Conservative without spirit

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the phrase from bottom to top
a block sits in the middle, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: taken as written
'I mean' is another way of saying I intend
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Someone plans to show up and obstruct a lacklustre Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without spirit' could suggest teetotal, but here it means lacking energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemic figuratively means feeble and lacking vigour, so lifeless or spiritless.

clue.text: Wary about overturning support for container of dangerous liquid

indicators.note: overturning flips the word, so in a down clue it reads upwards
'about' means going around the other piece

blocks.note: coy can mean reticent or wary
a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: A cautious person refuses to knock over the stand holding a hazardous liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: Coy usually means bashful; the sense here is reluctant to commit, hence wary.
explanation.definitionFit: A carboy is a large bottle, often in a crate, used for storing acids and other corrosive liquids.

clue.text: A cricket club almost entirely adopting rugby as additional item

indicators.note: almost means falling just short, so the last letter goes
adopting takes something in, so it goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
CC is the abbreviation for cricket club
RU stands for Rugby Union
all means entirely

explanation.surface: A cricket club nearly fully takes up rugby as an extra sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby letters go between the club abbreviation and the shortened word, not around the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: An accrual is something that accumulates or is added over time, such as interest.

clue.text: Small body of water, and reducing in size?

definitions.text: Small body of water, and reducing in size?

blocks.note: surface reading: a pond or little lake
setter's reading: a once huge inland sea that is small because it has been shrinking

explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' reads as a permanent size; here it means the water has become small, and is still shrinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The Central Asian lake, once among the world's largest, has shrunk drastically since rivers feeding it were diverted for irrigation.

clue.text: Seductress making for passion not love in lad

indicators.note: 'making for ... not' says one thing is swapped in where the other was

blocks.note: a son is a lad
ire is passionate anger
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A temptress who stirs up lust, rather than love, in a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace the O of SON with IRE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Sirens lured sailors with song, so a siren is a dangerously alluring woman.

clue.text: Neural centre developed in tribesman

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A nerve centre forming within a member of a tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: The brainstem joins brain to spinal cord and controls breathing and heartbeat, a core nerve centre.

clue.text: Beat most of the nick

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short
nick is British slang for steal, to rob

explanation.surface: A police beat covering most of the station, nick being British slang for a police station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' suggests a prison or police station; here it is the verb meaning steal.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a pulse or rhythmic beat, as of the heart.

clue.text: Former house, years old, with a couple of Kings

blocks.note: Y is the abbreviation for years
O is the abbreviation for old
R for rex and K for king, two abbreviations for king

explanation.surface: An ancient royal dynasty that produced a pair of monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' here means a royal dynasty, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of York was an English royal dynasty in the Wars of the Roses, now defunct.

clue.text: Medic losing a love, considering everything mostly as a matter of faith

indicators.note: losing something means it drops out of the word
mostly means all but the last letter

blocks.note: a doctor is a medic
love is zero, written O
'in all' means taking everything into account

explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from DOCTOR, then cut the last letter from IN ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctrinal means concerning doctrine, the set of beliefs a religion teaches.
